source.notes: Compiled from Monash University public web pages (blog + about-FODMAP pages, NOT the paid app database), Wikipedia FODMAP / Low-FODMAP diet pages, and secondary citations of Varney et al. 2017 for cut-off values. Ratings reflect the food at a typical serving as stated by the source; null means the source did not attribute that FODMAP group to the food. Where public sources disagree, the notes field says so; see monash-public-notes.md. Serving sizes are Monash-stated where given; "typical serve" means the source rated the food without a numeric portion.

foods.name: onion
foods.notes: Rated red even in very small amounts. Fructans are water-soluble, not fat-soluble: onion-infused oil is low FODMAP, but onion in soups/stocks leaches fructans. Microwaving in water reduced fructans 71% but did not make it low FODMAP.

foods.name: garlic
foods.notes: Garlic-infused oil is low FODMAP (fructans not fat-soluble). Garlic powder also high; "even very small amounts contribute significantly". Microwaving reduced fructans 57% but remained high/moderate.

foods.name: garlic-infused oil
foods.notes: Low FODMAP because fructans are not fat-soluble. Discard garlic pieces; commercial infused oils are the safer choice.

foods.name: garlic powder
foods.notes: Named exception to normal quantity rules: even very small amounts contribute significantly to FODMAP load.

foods.name: onion powder
foods.notes: Same exception as garlic powder.

foods.name: garlic scape
foods.notes: Curly stems of hardneck garlic; lower in fructans than the bulb. Gourmend garlic scape powder is Monash certified.

foods.name: leek
foods.notes: Listed high FODMAP (Monash food list, SE Asia post). Wikipedia: white part high fructans; green leaves are low FODMAP. Monash Asian-condiments post lists leek (leaves) as a low FODMAP flavouring.

foods.name: scallion
foods.lowServing: green tops only, any typical amount
foods.notes: Green part is low FODMAP and is Monash's standard onion substitute; the white bulb is high in fructans (Wikipedia; Monash eating-out post flags "spring onion" as high when whole).

foods.name: shallot
foods.notes: Swap for spring onion green tops. Fried shallots on Asian dishes are high.

foods.name: chive
foods.notes: Recommended onion replacement; add late in cooking.

foods.name: asafoetida
foods.notes: Indian spice used as onion-flavour substitute; potent smell.

foods.name: ginger
foods.notes: Low FODMAP; used as flavouring alternative to onion/garlic.

foods.name: artichoke
foods.notes: Listed high FODMAP (fructans) by Monash food list, gluten post, and Wikipedia.

foods.name: jerusalem artichoke
foods.notes: Wikipedia fructan source; Monash protein-powder post flags Jerusalem artichoke as a high FODMAP prebiotic ingredient.

foods.name: asparagus
foods.notes: Monash food list: high. Monash reintroduction post uses asparagus as an excess-fructose challenge food. Wikipedia lists fructans as moderate/portion-dependent.

foods.name: green pea
foods.notes: High GOS (Monash food list, enzyme posts; "thawed green peas" used as GOS source in Monash GOS trial).

foods.name: sugar snap pea
foods.notes: Listed high FODMAP on Monash about-FODMAP page; FODMAP group not stated in the public source (Wikipedia groups mange-tout/snow peas under polyols).

foods.name: snow pea
foods.notes: Wikipedia: polyol source. Monash recipe-modification post swaps snow peas out citing polyols/fructans; Monash stir-fry post lists snow peas among low-FODMAP options at app serve size.

foods.name: mushroom
foods.notes: Mannitol. Microwaving reduced mannitol 58% but still high/moderate.

foods.name: oyster mushroom
foods.notes: Listed low FODMAP in Monash shopping list and stir-fry post, unlike common mushrooms.

foods.name: cauliflower
foods.notes: Wikipedia: polyol (mannitol) source. Monash gentle-diet and recipe-modification posts list it as high; one summary said "oligosaccharides" but Monash retesting notes call out mannitol. Monash reintroduction update notes non-FODMAP components may also cause symptoms.

foods.name: red bell pepper
foods.lowServing: 75 g (1/4 medium) per pre-2024 fibre post
foods.notes: Rating changed after Monash's 2024 fructose cut-off review: now listed high (excess fructose) at a typical serve; older posts list 75 g as low. Step-3 post: OK if tolerant to excess fructose.

foods.name: green bell pepper
foods.notes: Low FODMAP; contains limited fructans at larger serves.

foods.name: eggplant
foods.notes: Green at standard serve; sorbitol accumulates at larger quantities.

foods.name: green bean
foods.notes: Low FODMAP (Wikipedia and many Monash posts).

foods.name: carrot
foods.lowServing: no upper limit ("even very large serves")
foods.notes: Monash: remains green in very large serves.

foods.name: potato
foods.notes: Monash: green with no upper limit.

foods.name: tomato
foods.notes: Low FODMAP. Cherry tomatoes contain excess fructose at higher serves (see cherry tomato).

foods.name: cherry tomato
foods.lowServing: 45 g (3 tomatoes); 6 pieces used in Monash recipe
foods.notes: Contains fructose at higher serves.

foods.name: sweet potato
foods.notes: Mannitol drives amber/red at larger serves.

foods.name: red cabbage
foods.notes: Fructans at larger serves.

foods.name: white cabbage
foods.notes: Monash shopping list: red or white cabbage low at 1 serve. Wikipedia: cabbage polyols moderate/portion-dependent. Fermented into sauerkraut it becomes high (mannitol).

foods.name: savoy cabbage
foods.notes: Wikipedia fructan source. Monash reintroduction update notes non-FODMAP components may also cause symptoms.

foods.name: brussels sprout
foods.notes: Monash: 75 g considered high in fructans; named as fructan source in gluten post; Wikipedia agrees.

foods.name: butternut squash
foods.notes: Used as a GOS-rich food in Monash GOS enzyme trial.

foods.name: beet
foods.notes: Wikipedia: fructan source; Monash GOS trial used beetroot as a GOS source. Pickled beet is low at 1 serve (shopping list).

foods.name: broccoli
foods.lowServing: 1 cup whole or heads only (75 g)
foods.notes: Excess fructose is the main FODMAP; concentrated in the stalks (see broccoli stalk).

foods.name: broccoli stalk
foods.notes: Stalks-only are high at 1 cup; heads-only and whole broccoli are low.

foods.name: broccolini
foods.lowServing: 21 g heads (post-2024 cut-off); stalks 1 cup low
foods.notes: Green serve for heads reduced from 58 g to 21 g after the 2024 fructose cut-off change. Stalks-only are low at 1 cup.

foods.name: corn
foods.notes: Monash endurance post: polyols/oligosaccharides; low at <=43 g, 85 g high. Vegetables post: 1 cob high, 1/2 cob green/amber.

foods.name: turnip
foods.notes: Listed among high-soluble-fibre low FODMAP vegetables.

foods.name: kohlrabi
foods.notes: Example of a food green even at very large serves.

foods.name: fennel
foods.notes: Wikipedia lists fennel as moderate (portion-dependent) for both fructans and polyols. Fennel seed is low (Monash herbs post).

foods.name: chicory
foods.notes: Leaves moderate polyols per Wikipedia. Chicory ROOT extract/inulin is high fructans (see inulin).

foods.name: bean sprouts
foods.notes: Sprouted mung beans are low FODMAP (Wikipedia; Monash sprouting post: mung bean red to green after sprouting).

foods.name: sauerkraut
foods.notes: Raw cabbage is low, but fermentation produces mannitol. Red cabbage sauerkraut tested moderate; smaller low serve in app.

foods.name: pickled vegetables
foods.notes: Tested high; smaller serve in app. Group not stated.

foods.name: chili pepper
foods.lowServing: typical amount (1/2 red chilli 14 g in meal plan)
foods.notes: Low FODMAP, but capsaicin is a non-FODMAP trigger for some; Monash advises limiting.

foods.name: apple
foods.notes: Excess fructose + sorbitol. Apple juice also high. Microwaving reduced FODMAPs only 26%.

foods.name: pear
foods.notes: Excess fructose + sorbitol; pear juice high.

foods.name: mango
foods.notes: Contains only excess fructose, so Monash uses it as the fructose challenge food. Low FODMAP at a small serve if fructose-tolerant (step 3 post).

foods.name: watermelon
foods.notes: Monash gentle-diet post: fructose; Wikipedia: polyol source. Honeydew is the low swap.

foods.name: cherry
foods.notes: Stone fruit; sorbitol (Monash polyols post).

foods.name: prune
foods.notes: Wikipedia polyol source; dried fruit is high in excess fructose (Monash processing post).

foods.name: lychee
foods.notes: Fresh lychee is a polyol source (Wikipedia); canned lychee is listed low by Monash.

foods.name: dried fruit
foods.notes: Generic Monash listing: high. Exceptions with tested low serves: dried cranberry (9 g), goji (10 g), raisins (small serve), banana chips.

foods.name: raisin
foods.notes: Listed as a low FODMAP insoluble-fibre source in a Monash post; generic dried fruit is high, so serving size matters.

foods.name: dried cranberry
foods.notes: Contains oligo-fructans; fresh/frozen cranberries untested per recipe post.

foods.name: unripe banana
foods.notes: Firm bananas are low FODMAP.

foods.name: ripe banana
foods.notes: Re-tested: ripe bananas accumulate fructans (cold storage stress). Monash: no need to remove if currently tolerated.

foods.name: strawberry
foods.notes: Retested with increased fructose; still low at 1 serve, OK at larger serves if fructose-tolerant.

foods.name: green kiwifruit
foods.notes: Zespri green and SunGold certified low FODMAP at 2 fruit.

foods.name: honeydew melon
foods.notes: Low FODMAP; Wikipedia contrasts with watermelon (high). Monash Singapore post lists as low.

foods.name: grape
foods.notes: Retested with increased fructose; still low at 1 serve; larger serves need fructose tolerance.

foods.name: guava
foods.notes: Ripeness flips the rating: well-ripened low, unripe high.

foods.name: avocado
foods.notes: Monash later found the polyol is perseitol rather than sorbitol; rating kept red at standard serve. High fat is an additional trigger.

foods.name: coconut
foods.notes: Fresh flesh low; dried shredded coconut moderate at 1/2 cup, 1 tbsp fine.

foods.name: coconut water
foods.notes: Fructans and sorbitol at larger serves.

foods.name: bilberry
foods.notes: Preliminary Monash analysis.

foods.name: lingonberry
foods.notes: Preliminary Monash analysis.

foods.name: custard apple
foods.notes: Used as a GOS source in Monash GOS enzyme trial.

foods.name: fruit juice concentrate
foods.notes: Label red flag for excess fructose.

foods.name: wheat bread
foods.notes: Fructans (and some GOS). Wholemeal bread green at 1 slice, red at 2.

foods.name: wheat pasta
foods.notes: Used by Monash as the "fructans in grains" challenge food.

foods.name: wheat noodles
foods.notes: Rice noodles are the low swap.

foods.name: rye
foods.notes: Sprouting reduces but rye bread/crispbread listed high.

foods.name: barley
foods.notes: Sprouted barley grain went red to green in Monash sprouting study.

foods.name: spelt
foods.highServing: typical serve (spelt flakes, modern-process spelt bread)
foods.notes: Lower fructan than modern wheat but only traditional sourdough spelt bread tests low.

foods.name: spelt sourdough bread
foods.notes: >12 h traditional ferment reduces fructans. Certified brands listed in app.

foods.name: gluten-free bread
foods.notes: Low because GF flours are low FODMAP; check for high FODMAP add-ins (honey, inulin).

foods.name: oats
foods.lowServing: 1/2 cup uncooked (52 g); 1/4 cup in gluten post
foods.notes: "Relatively low in FODMAPs" (FAQ). Oat bran also low.

foods.name: oat milk
foods.notes: Used as a GOS source in Monash GOS trial; Italy post lists it among lactose-free alternatives (small serve).

foods.name: rice
foods.notes: Naturally very low; no stacking concern (Monash).

foods.name: rice milk
foods.notes: Moved from red to green after improved lab methods; small fructans remain, avoid excessive quantities.

foods.name: corn flakes
foods.notes: Gluten-free corn flakes listed low.

foods.name: bulgur
foods.notes: Wheat-derived but low at this serve.

foods.name: freekeh
foods.notes: Used as a GOS source in Monash GOS trial.

foods.name: couscous
foods.notes: Only the gluten-free variety is listed low; wheat couscous not covered.

foods.name: wheat muesli
foods.notes: Wheat- and fruit-free muesli is a low swap (diabetes post); honey/dried fruit add fructose.

foods.name: pastry
foods.notes: Wheat-flour pastries/croissants/cakes listed high in Italy post.

foods.name: wonton wrapper
foods.notes: Wheat wrappers; SE Asia post: gyoza, mandu, wontons, bao, man tou likely moderate-high.

foods.name: pretzel
foods.notes: Listed among low FODMAP snacks; wheat-based so serving matters.

foods.name: chickpea
foods.highServing: dried/boiled typical serve; 125 g small can used in Monash recipes
foods.notes: Canning leaches oligos. Microwaving 3 min in water brought chickpeas to green. Sprouting slightly increased FODMAPs.

foods.name: chickpea flour
foods.notes: Label red flag for oligosaccharides.

foods.name: lentil
foods.lowServing: 1/2 cup canned; 1/4 cup boiled green lentil (23 g)
foods.notes: Canned lentils are low (Wikipedia, Monash).

foods.name: butter bean
foods.lowServing: 1/4 cup canned (42 g); 35 g for baked beans

foods.name: mung bean
foods.lowServing: 1/4 cup boiled and drained (53 g); sprouted mung beans low
foods.notes: Sprouting moved mung beans from red to green.

foods.name: red kidney bean
foods.notes: Contains both fructans and GOS. Sprouting reduced FODMAPs.

foods.name: hummus
foods.notes: Also usually contains garlic.

foods.name: soybean
foods.notes: Processing to soy protein isolate removes GOS.

foods.name: soy milk (whole bean)
aliases: soy milk made from whole soybeans
foods.notes: Used as GOS source in Monash trial; soy cappuccino likewise.

foods.name: soy milk (soy protein)
foods.notes: GOS removed during protein extraction.

foods.name: firm tofu
foods.notes: Drained firm tofu is low; water-soluble FODMAPs are pressed out.

foods.name: silken tofu
foods.notes: High water content retains GOS and fructans.

foods.name: soy lecithin
foods.notes: Not formally tested; considered low because it is fat-based and used in tiny amounts.

foods.name: almond
foods.notes: Wikipedia: maximum 10 per serving. Almond meal low at 1/4 cup (24 g). Almond milk low (diluted).

foods.name: almond milk
foods.notes: Low despite almonds being GOS-containing because the milk is dilute; choose calcium-fortified.

foods.name: cashew
foods.notes: High GOS (and fructans per Monash fructan post).

foods.name: mixed nuts
foods.notes: Assumes mix excludes cashews/pistachios.

foods.name: chia seed
foods.notes: Some anecdotal intolerance (Monash superfoods post).

foods.name: tahini
foods.notes: Contains fructans/GOS at higher serves.

foods.name: cow milk
foods.notes: Only a problem for lactose-intolerant people (label post). Most lactose-intolerant people tolerate 12-15 g lactose/day spread out (about 250 ml).

foods.name: yogurt
foods.lowServing: small serve; 200 g/day in Mediterranean post for tolerant
foods.notes: Cow's milk yogurt tested high in fermented-foods post. Lactose-free yogurt is the swap.

foods.name: cream
foods.notes: Cream-based sauces flagged high in Italy post.

foods.name: cream cheese
foods.notes: Lactose-free cream cheese low (lunchbox post).

foods.name: parmesan
foods.lowServing: typical serve (1 tbsp shaved in recipe)

foods.name: gouda
foods.notes: Plain Gouda essentially lactose-free; flavoured versions may contain garlic.

foods.name: mozzarella
foods.notes: Italy post: standard mozzarella acceptable in small quantities; lactose-free versions available.

foods.name: butter
foods.notes: 80%+ fat, negligible lactose.

foods.name: custard
foods.notes: Lactose-free custard is low (lunchbox post).

foods.name: whey protein concentrate
foods.notes: Lactose in concentrate; plant protein powders may contain GOS/fructans (untested).

foods.name: dark chocolate
foods.notes: High fat can still trigger symptoms.

foods.name: egg
foods.lowServing: no FODMAP limit (41 g egg has 0.3 g carbohydrate)

foods.name: chicken
foods.notes: Marinated versions may contain garlic, honey, applesauce.

foods.name: fish
foods.notes: Canned unflavoured fish low.

foods.name: ham
foods.notes: Plain cured ham listed low in Monash posts; check processed meats for garlic/onion.

foods.name: salami
foods.notes: Flagged because it often contains garlic; plain versions not rated in public sources.

foods.name: marinated meat
foods.notes: Monash food list: "some marinated meats" high (garlic, honey, apple sauce).

foods.name: processed meat
foods.notes: Monash food list: "some processed meats" high (onion/garlic, wheat fillers). Group inferred from ingredients named in Monash posts.

foods.name: honey
foods.highServing: 2 tbsp recipe amount; 1.5-2 tsp used as day-1/2 challenge doses
foods.notes: Maple syrup is the swap.

foods.name: high fructose corn syrup
foods.notes: Avoid if sensitive to excess fructose.

foods.name: maple syrup
foods.notes: Monash food list and recipe posts: low. One older flavour post summarised it as "moderate"; treat as low at typical serve.

foods.name: table sugar
foods.notes: Glucose+fructose 1:1, no excess fructose.

foods.name: coconut sugar
foods.notes: Monash sugar post cautions coconut sugar "may contain FODMAPs" and directs to the app; not a clean rating.

foods.name: sorbitol
foods.highServing: as sweetener; 10 g dose triggers symptoms in IBS

foods.name: mannitol
foods.highServing: as sweetener; 10 g dose triggers symptoms in IBS

foods.name: erythritol
foods.notes: Label-reading post lists erythritol as LOW (well absorbed); the sweeteners post groups it with polyols to be cautious about. Sources disagree.

foods.name: glycerol
foods.notes: Acceptable during restrictive phase per Monash additives post.

foods.name: inulin
foods.notes: Purified fructan; even very small amounts contribute significantly.

foods.name: sugar-free confectionery
foods.notes: Sweetened with polyols in high doses.

foods.name: jam
foods.notes: Raspberry jam green at 40 g with fructans at higher serves; strawberry jam and marmalade listed low. Check for HFCS/apple juice concentrate.

foods.name: coffee
foods.notes: Low FODMAP but caffeine stimulates the gut (non-FODMAP trigger). Milk additions add lactose.

foods.name: green tea
foods.notes: Low FODMAP; contains caffeine.

foods.name: water
foods.notes: Carbonation can distend the gut (non-FODMAP).

foods.name: soda
foods.lowServing: typical serve if sugar-sweetened with sucrose
foods.notes: Listed low FODMAP in non-FODMAP triggers post; carbonation is a mechanical trigger. HFCS-sweetened sodas would be high fructose (see HFCS).

foods.name: kombucha
foods.notes: Commercial products tested; contains fructans.

foods.name: kvass
foods.notes: Cereal-based fermented drink tested low.

foods.name: red wine
foods.lowServing: up to 250 ml (<100 ml/day in Mediterranean post)
foods.notes: Group not stated in public post.

foods.name: white wine
foods.notes: Non-FODMAP triggers post: wine low FODMAP; alcohol itself is a gut irritant. FAQ: "low GI" sweet wines are high in fructose.

foods.name: dessert wine
foods.notes: Tested high; FAQ attributes sweet/low-GI wine to fructose.

foods.name: rum
foods.notes: Tested high in FODMAPs; group not stated publicly.

foods.name: spirits
foods.notes: Non-FODMAP triggers post: spirits low FODMAP (rum is the tested exception). Alcohol is a gut irritant.

foods.name: soy sauce
foods.lowServing: 2 tsp (10 g) in meal plan; typical serve

foods.name: hoisin sauce
foods.moderateServing: small amount rated moderate in dietitian day-on-plate
foods.notes: Sources disagree; treat as low only in small amounts.

foods.name: sweet chili sauce
foods.notes: Rated moderate in Monash dietitian post.

foods.name: barbecue sauce
foods.notes: Check for onion/garlic/HFCS.

foods.name: pesto
foods.notes: Garlic drives the rating.

foods.name: curry paste
foods.notes: Shallot/garlic-based pastes high.

foods.name: stock
foods.highServing: regular stock (contains onion/garlic; fructans leach into water)

foods.name: olive oil
foods.lowServing: no FODMAPs (60 ml/day in Mediterranean post)

foods.name: sorbet
foods.notes: Depends on fruit used; Italy post lists as suitable option.

foods.name: bitterballen
foods.notes: Onion-containing; untested, judged from ingredients.

foods.name: stroopwafel
foods.notes: Judged low-moderate from ingredients (wheat), untested.

foods.name: laksa
foods.notes: Onion/garlic/shallot-based dish.

foods.name: curry powder
foods.notes: Listed low in Monash herbs guide; Monash flavour post warns seasoning blends may contain onion/garlic - check labels.
